# Rules

<!-- Generated by `toolism rules --format markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Rules run in id order. `SL0xx` rules are **safe**: they never change which tool calls
validate and only drop information the model already has. `SL1xx` rules are lossy for
annotations and run with `--level annotations`. Turn any rule on or off with `--enable` /
`--disable` (by id or name), and set options with `--option RULE.key=value`.

| [`SL002`](#sl002-nullable-anyof) | nullable-anyof | safe | default |

| [`SL004`](#sl004-inline-defs) | inline-defs | safe | default |

| [`SL009`](#sl009-schema-uri) | schema-uri | safe | default |

## SL001 redundant-title

**Drop titles that only repeat the property, $defs key or tool name.**

`title` is an annotation. Pydantic and FastMCP add one to every property and model, set to
the property name ("User Id" for `user_id`) or the model/function name — information the
model already has from the property key or tool name. Informative titles are kept.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL002 nullable-anyof

**Rewrite anyOf/oneOf of bare {type} branches as a type array.**

`Optional[X]` in Pydantic becomes `anyOf` of two one-keyword branches. A `type` array
accepts exactly the same instances and is shorter. For `oneOf` the rewrite is only equivalent
when no instance can match two branches, so overlapping types (`integer`/`number`) are left
alone. Note: rewriting to plain `X` would reject an explicit `null` — never do that.

`date | None` arrives as `anyOf: [{type: string, format: date}, {type: null}]`. The
string-only keywords `format`, `pattern`, `minLength` and `maxLength` are hoisted onto
the merged node, which is equivalent only when exactly one branch is `type: string` and no
other branch can be a string. If the node already carries one of those keywords, or a branch
has any other keyword, the node is left alone.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL003 null-default

**Drop default: null on properties that are not required.**

`default` is an annotation with no effect on validation. On a property that is not
`required`, `default: null` only restates "you may leave this out", which the missing
`required` entry already says. Skipped for strict tools (every property is required there).

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL004 inline-defs

**Inline $defs used exactly once and delete unused $defs.**

Generators put every nested model in `$defs` and reference it, even when it is used once.
Inlining removes the `$defs` wrapper and the `$ref` string. Conservative by design
(architecture review R2): never inlines recursive, pinned or multi-use definitions, never when
other JSON pointers exist, never `$ref` siblings under draft <= 7, and never when keywords
other than annotations would collide.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL005 description-whitespace

**Dedent docstrings, strip trailing spaces, collapse blank lines and space runs.**

Python docstrings arrive indented, with blank lines and trailing spaces. Every whitespace
token costs input tokens. Only whitespace changes; leading indentation that marks nested list
structure is kept.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL006 echo-description

**Drop property descriptions whose words only repeat the property name.**

`user_id: "The user ID."` tells the model nothing the key `user_id` didn't. The match is
exact on content words (case styles split, stop-words removed), so any extra word — "Unique
user ID" — keeps the description. Tool-level descriptions are never touched.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL007 stable-order

**Sort tools by name (0 tokens saved; keeps prompt-cache prefixes stable).**

Saves no tokens by itself. Agents that assemble tools from several MCP servers often send
them in a different order on each request, which breaks provider prompt caching (cached reads
cost ~10% of normal input). Off by default because tool order can be intentional.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: `--enable SL007`
- Reorders tools; applied after all content rules.

## SL008 noop-keywords

**Drop no-op keywords (required: [], additionalProperties: true, ...).**

Each of these is exactly the default and changes nothing: `required: []`,
`description: ""`, empty `$defs`, `additionalProperties: true` (and friends),
`items: {}` / `items: true`. `type: ["x"]` becomes `"x"`. `properties: {}` is kept on
purpose — OpenAI rejects object schemas without it. Strict tools keep `required` and
`additional*` keywords.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL009 schema-uri

**Drop the root $schema URI when the schema is dialect-invariant.**

zod-to-json-schema and many MCP servers add `"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/
schema#"` to every tool — 10-15 tokens each that the model has no use for. Without
`$schema` validators assume 2020-12, so the URI is only dropped when nothing in the schema
behaves differently between the declared draft and 2020-12. Draft-04 is never touched.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL010 single-allof

**Collapse single-branch allOf when merging preserves validation.**

A single `allOf` branch can be merged into its parent when their keywords are
independent. Duplicate keywords (including annotations) are never overwritten. Groups
that depend on sibling keywords, such as `properties`/`additionalProperties` and
`if`/`then`/`else`, must stay on one side of the boundary. Unevaluated keywords,
unknown keywords and moved definition containers are left alone.

Strict tools, unknown or nested dialects, dynamic scopes and references other than
root-definition pointers are skipped. This keeps reference targets and scope intact.
Under draft <= 7 a branch's `$ref` is only hoisted when it gains no siblings; a parent
`$ref` is left alone. Keyword order and all annotation values are preserved.

- Safety: `safe` — Validation-equivalent; removes only provably redundant information.
- Enabled by: default

## SL101 max-description-length

**Truncate descriptions longer than max_chars at a sentence boundary.**

Long descriptions (pasted API docs, examples, caveats) are often the biggest part of a tool
definition. Truncating them loses information the model might use, so this rule is lossy and
opt-in. Tool-level descriptions are only truncated with `include_tool=true`.

- Safety: `annotations` — Validation-equivalent, but may drop annotation text the model could use.
- Enabled by: `--level annotations`

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `max_chars` | int | `300` | maximum characters per description |
| `include_tool` | bool | `false` | also truncate the tool-level description |

## SL102 drop-examples

**Remove examples / example keywords from schemas.**

Examples are annotations: dropping them never changes validation, but they can help the
model produce well-formed arguments — measure before and after on your own evals.

- Safety: `annotations` — Validation-equivalent, but may drop annotation text the model could use.
- Enabled by: `--level annotations`

## SL103 drop-titles

**Drop all schema title annotations.**

`title` is an annotation keyword, so removing it never changes validation. This lossy
rule is for users who prefer smaller schemas over retaining display labels. Property names are
schema keys rather than `title` keywords and are therefore never removed.

- Safety: `annotations` — Validation-equivalent, but may drop annotation text the model could use.
- Enabled by: `--level annotations`
